objects.description: Abstract base class for pattern matching engines. Manages input buffering, iteration over matches, line/column tracking, and exposes a virtual match() plus capture/group APIs for concrete engines.

Specialization of PatternMatcher for std::string patterns. Manages a heap-allocated std::string when constructed from a string, or refers to an external std::string when provided as a pointer.

A Unicode tables provider specialized for regex/character-class handling, derived from reflex::Posix::Tables. It encapsulates Unicode block/script/letter tables and a composition map for normalization. Provides static case-mapping helpers and internal initialization routines. Input is a unified input source wrapper that reads bytes as ASCII/UTF-8 from strings, wide strings (converting to UTF-8), FILE*, or std::istream. It supports encoding detection/translation (BOM-aware, several codepages), optional FILE* handler callbacks, and utility nested streambufs. Move-like copy semantics: copying shares state, so do not read from both copies. Some methods (file_init, file_size, etc.) are only declared here and defined elsewhere.
Abstract functor interface to handle FILE* reads: can inspect/modify buffer and size, handle errors, support non-blocking IO. Assign via Input::set_handler().
A std::streambuf adaptor that exposes an Input as an unbuffered std::istream source. Reads via Input::get().
A std::streambuf adaptor that normalizes DOS CRLF to LF while reading from an Input. Useful for legacy DOS text files.
Input subclass that adds an internal fixed-size buffer to provide efficient peek/get and to back std::streambuf adaptors. Exposes same unified sources, with buffering on top.
std::streambuf adaptor backed by BufferedInput (or Input), providing buffered extraction for std::istream usage.
Buffered std::streambuf adaptor that converts CRLF to LF while reading from BufferedInput or Input sources.

Alias type defined by this header as reflex::timer_type. On Windows builds, timer_type is a typedef of the Windows API SYSTEMTIME structure and is used with timer_start() and timer_elapsed() to measure elapsed wall-clock time in milliseconds. Wraps every 60 seconds. Construction is by passing a timer_type lvalue to timer_start(). Destruction is trivial; no resources are owned.

Alias type defined by this header as reflex::timer_type. On non-Windows builds, timer_type is a typedef of the POSIX timeval structure and is used with timer_start() and timer_elapsed() to measure elapsed wall-clock time in milliseconds with microsecond precision. Wraps every 60 seconds. Construction is by passing a timer_type lvalue to timer_start(). Destruction is trivial; no resources are owned.

POSIX character class tables holder. Provides a map from POSIX class name strings to pointers to integer arrays describing contiguous [lo,hi] character ranges. The map uses a custom comparator (lt) that orders keys by strcmp. The class exposes a default constructor (defined elsewhere) and a public member 'range' for access. Destruction/ownership details for the pointed-to int arrays are not specified here; likely static or externally managed.
Comparator functor for ordering C-string keys in std::map by strcmp. Used by Tables::Range.

objects.definition: typedef std::map<const char*,const int*,lt> Range;
objects.description: Alias type for the map used by Tables to associate POSIX class name strings with pointers to integer range tables. Keys are const char*; values are const int* pointing to [lo,hi] pairs; comparator is Tables::lt.

Primary regex pattern compiler and container for RE/flex. It stores the pattern text, compiler options, internal DFA/HFA structures, and either generated opcode table or an FSM function for use by reflex::Matcher. Provides construction from regex strings or precompiled code/FSM, timing stats, introspection (states/edges/words), and fast search prediction helpers. Many helper types (nested structs/enums/typedefs) are internal implementation details. Construction is via constructors or assign(); destruction automatically frees owned opcode arrays when allocated. Details like regex_error_type and ORanges<> are referenced from other headers.
Compile-time constants used by Pattern for opcode encoding, table sizes, and predict-match parameters.

C++11 std::regex-backed matcher implementing the reflex::PatternMatcher interface. Provides scan/find/split/match over buffered input, management of pattern sources (std::regex or pattern strings), capture-group inspection, and cloning. Uses std::cregex_iterator and std::regex match flags. Destruction/ownership: may allocate internal std::regex when pattern(const char*)/pattern(const std::string&) are used, tracked by own_; otherwise uses shared Pattern pointers.

Specialized StdMatcher constrained to ECMAScript syntax (std::regex::ECMAScript). Constructors accept regex strings or existing std::regex patterns; asserts that provided std::regex is not POSIX flavored. Manages internal pattern ownership when constructed from strings.

Specialized StdMatcher for POSIX ERE (std::regex::awk) syntax. Provides the same matching interface but asserts that patterns are POSIX ERE flavored. Includes a tailored convert() for POSIX-compatible escapes. Manages internal std::regex when created from strings.

A concrete matcher engine that implements AbstractMatcher to match input by lines only. It provides scan, find, split, and match behaviors with options: A to include the trailing newline in FIND matches, N to also return empty lines with FIND, and X (noted in comments as W; implemented as X) to return only empty lines with FIND. It maintains internal state to optionally skip over a newline between finds. Construction mirrors AbstractMatcher: from an Input and optional option string.

Fuzzy regular-expression matcher implementing approximate matching on top of reflex::Matcher. Supports configurable maximum edit distance and options to permit insertions, deletions, substitutions, and binary (byte-wise) matching. Provides scan/find/split/match behavior and reports the number of edits taken for a match.

reflex::Matcher is a concrete regular-expression matcher engine implementing the PatternMatcher<reflex::Pattern> interface. It supports scan/find/split/match operations, indentation-aware tokens, SIMD-accelerated advance routines, and exposes APIs to manage indent stops and group captures. Construction accepts an existing Pattern, a regex string, or std::string, plus an Input source and options. Memory ownership: by default shares Pattern; clone creates a new Matcher copying state but sharing pattern. Destruction/cleanup is managed by standard C++ semantics; no explicit destructor defined here.

functions.name: reflex::Bits::operator|

functions.name: reflex::Bits::operator&

functions.name: reflex::Bits::operator^

functions.name: reflex::Bits::operator-

functions.description: Lexicographic greater-than, implemented as bits.operator<(*this).

functions.name: reflex::Bits::any

functions.description: Returns the logical size in bits, equal to the number of allocated 64-bit words multiplied by 64 (len_ << 6).

functions.name: reflex::Bits::count

functions.name: reflex::Bits::intersects

functions.name: reflex::Bits::contains

requirements: bits must be a valid initialized reflex::Bits.

functions.name: reflex::Bits::find_first

functions.name: reflex::is_disjoint
functions.signature:
template <typename S1, typename S2>
bool is_disjoint(const S1& s1, const S2& s2);
functions.description: Returns true if the two ordered containers s1 and s2 are disjoint (no common element), otherwise false. Intended for ordered set-like containers supporting iteration in sorted order and a comparator compatible with S1::key_compare. Efficiently walks both containers in order to detect any equal elements.
requirements: S1 and S2 must be ordered associative containers (or behave like them) providing: empty(), begin(), end(), rbegin(), key_comp().
The comparator S1::key_compare must be callable with values dereferenced from both S1 and S2; i.e., S2's element type must be comparable with S1's key type using S1::key_compare.
Both s1 and s2 must remain valid during the call and not be modified concurrently.

requirements: S must provide find(const T&) and end() returning an iterator comparable to the result of find().
The lookup T must be acceptable by S::find; i.e., S must have a compatible key_equal/Compare and key type for T.
s must remain valid during the call and not be modified concurrently.

requirements: S1 and S2 must be ordered associative containers (or behave like them) providing: empty(), begin(), end(), rbegin(), key_comp().
S1::key_compare must be able to compare elements from S1 and S2; i.e., S2's element type must be comparable with S1's key type using S1::key_compare.
s1 and s2 must remain valid during the call and not be modified concurrently.

requirements: S1 must be assignable from S2 (S1::operator=(const S2&)) if s1 may be empty at call time; otherwise, S1 must provide insert(InputIterator, InputIterator).
S2 must provide begin() and end() returning iterators over its elements.
Element types of S2 must be insertable into S1 (compatible key/value types and comparator).
s1 and s2 must remain valid during the call and s1 must not be concurrently modified.

s1 and s2 must remain valid during the call and must not be concurrently modified.

functions.signature: std::string reflex::latin1(int a, int b, int esc = 'x', bool brackets = true);
functions.description: Builds a regular-expression fragment that matches the UTF-8 encoding of an 8-bit ASCII/Latin-1 code-point range [a,b]. Use esc = 'x' for hex escapes (\xXX) or '0'/\0 for octal; set brackets to true to wrap the result in [...] character-class brackets. Intended for composing regexes that target UTF-8 strings while specifying ranges in Latin-1.
requirements: a and b define an inclusive range of 8-bit code points; a <= b is expected (behavior is unspecified otherwise).
esc should be either 'x' (hex) or '0'/\0 (octal) as implied by the documentation.
No memory ownership or lifetime constraints; returned std::string is self-contained.
No side effects; thread-safety depends on standard library string operations.

functions.name: reflex::utf8
functions.signature: std::string reflex::utf8(int a, int b, int esc = 'x', const char* par = "(", bool strict = true);
functions.description: Builds a regex fragment that matches the UTF-8 encoding of a UCS-4 code-point range [a,b]. The esc parameter selects hex ('x') vs octal ('0'/\0) escapes. The par parameter controls the parenthesis prefix to use (e.g., "(" for capturing or "(?:" for non-capturing). If strict is true, the produced pattern targets strict UTF-8; if false, it is more permissive/lean.
requirements: a and b define an inclusive UCS-4 range; a <= b is expected (behavior is unspecified otherwise).
par must point to a valid, null-terminated C string and must remain valid for the duration of the call; a typical value is "(" or "(?:".
esc should be either 'x' (hex) or '0'/\0 (octal) as implied by the documentation.
The function returns a self-contained std::string; no additional resource management required.

functions.name: reflex::wcs
functions.signature: std::wstring reflex::wcs(const char* s, size_t n);
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 byte sequence of length n starting at s into a wide string. On platforms with 2-byte wchar_t, outputs UTF-16 (including surrogate pairs for code points > U+FFFF). Invalid or out-of-range code points are mapped to U+FFFD. On platforms with 4-byte wchar_t, writes code points directly.
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of at least n bytes; it need not be NUL-terminated.
Behavior for invalid UTF-8 is to substitute U+FFFD for out-of-range code points; callers should not assume strict rejection.
Thread safety depends on the absence of shared mutable state; function uses only local variables.
s may be null only if n == 0; otherwise s must be non-null.

functions.name: reflex::wcs
functions.description: Converts an entire std::string containing UTF-8 into a std::wstring. Semantics mirror the const char*/length overload: produces UTF-16 with surrogate pairs when sizeof(wchar_t) == 2, otherwise UTF-32-like values; invalid/out-of-range inputs map to U+FFFD.
requirements: Input s is treated as a UTF-8 byte sequence; invalid code units are mapped to U+FFFD rather than causing errors.
No special lifetime or ownership requirements; returns a self-contained std::wstring.
Thread safety depends on standard library usage; function uses no global state.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::Tables::Tables
functions.description: Constructor for the Unicode Tables class. Initializes internal Unicode/Posix tables and mappings used by this component. Details of initialization are not documented in this header.
requirements: No explicit preconditions.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::Tables::toupper
functions.description: Static Unicode-aware uppercase mapping associated with Unicode::Tables. Converts a Unicode code point to its uppercase equivalent using the Tables’ data. Specific behavior for non-alphabetic code points is not documented; likely returns the input unchanged when no mapping exists (not explicitly stated).
requirements: c must represent a Unicode code point as an int.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::Tables::tolower
functions.description: Static Unicode-aware lowercase mapping associated with Unicode::Tables. Converts a Unicode code point to its lowercase equivalent using the Tables’ data. Specific behavior for non-alphabetic code points is not documented; likely returns the input unchanged when no mapping exists (not explicitly stated).
requirements: c must represent a Unicode code point as an int.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::range
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a table entry describing a [lo, hi] inclusive range of Unicode characters for the given Unicode class name. Returns NULL when the class name is not recognized.
requirements: The argument must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated C string naming a Unicode class.
Callers must check for a NULL return before dereferencing the returned pointer.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is not documented; treat it as an internal table entry that must not be freed or modified (inferred from return type).

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::compose
functions.description: Normalizes by composing two adjacent Unicode code points (prev, next) into a single composed code point. Returns -1 when the pair has no composition.
requirements: Both arguments must represent Unicode code points as ints.
Arguments are ordered as prev and next (corresponding to adjacent characters).
Callers must check for a return value of -1 to detect that no composition exists.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::toupper
functions.description: Unicode-aware uppercase mapping. Converts a Unicode code point to its uppercase equivalent. Part of the set of functions providing Unicode case translations.
requirements: c must represent a Unicode code point as an int.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::tolower
functions.description: Unicode-aware lowercase mapping. Converts a Unicode code point to its lowercase equivalent. Part of the set of functions providing Unicode case translations.
requirements: c must represent a Unicode code point as an int.

functions.name: reflex::Unicode::invcase
functions.description: Unicode case inversion. Intended to convert a Unicode code point to the opposite case (upper to lower or lower to upper). Exact behavior for non-alphabetic code points is not documented and may return the input unchanged (inferred).
requirements: c must represent a Unicode code point as an int.

functions.name: reflex::have_HW_AVX512BW
functions.description: Returns true if the CPU feature bitmap (reflex::HW) indicates AVX-512BW support. Intended for fast feature gating of SIMD code paths.
requirements: Available only when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2 defined (the section that defines reflex::HW and these helpers).

functions.name: reflex::have_HW_AVX2

requirements: Available only when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2 defined.
reflex::HW must be initialized before calling.

functions.name: reflex::ctz
functions.description: Counts the number of trailing zero bits in x and returns that count. Thin wrapper around platform intrinsics (__builtin_ctz or _BitScanForward).
requirements: Argument x must be nonzero; behavior is undefined for x == 0 (both __builtin_ctz and _BitScanForward do not define results for zero).

This inline is defined when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2. On ARM/NEON, a similarly named function may exist outside the reflex namespace and only when __ARM_ACLE and __ARM_FEATURE_CLZ are defined.

functions.name: reflex::popcount
functions.description: Returns the population count (number of set bits) of x. Uses __popcnt on MSVC or __builtin_popcount on GCC/Clang.
requirements: Defined when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2.
Accepts any 32-bit value; no special constraints.

functions.description: Counts the number of trailing zero bits in a 64-bit value and returns that count. Wraps __builtin_ctzl or _BitScanForward64 depending on compiler.
requirements: Argument x must be nonzero; behavior is undefined for x == 0 (both __builtin_ctzl and _BitScanForward64 do not define results for zero).

Defined when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2. On ARM/NEON, a similarly named function may exist outside the reflex namespace and only when __ARM_ACLE and __ARM_FEATURE_CLZ are defined.

functions.name: reflex::popcountl
functions.description: Returns the population count (number of set bits) of a 64-bit value. Uses __popcnt64 on MSVC or __builtin_popcountl on GCC/Clang.
requirements: Defined when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2.
Accepts any 64-bit value; no special constraints.

functions.name: reflex::simd_nlcount_avx2

functions.description: AVX2-accelerated partial newline counter. Counts newline characters in the memory range [b, e) and advances b close to e to indicate the remaining, uncounted tail. Intended to be called in a loop until b reaches e.
requirements: Declared only when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2; implemented for AVX2-capable builds.
b must reference a valid pointer into a readable memory buffer; e must point to the end (one past last) of the same buffer, with b <= e.
The memory range [b, e) must be accessible for reading.
Caller should expect b to be updated (advanced) on return and must use the updated b in subsequent calls to continue processing.

functions.signature: extern size_t reflex::simd_nlcount_avx512bw(const char *& b, const char *e)
functions.description: AVX-512BW-accelerated partial newline counter. Counts newline characters in [b, e) and advances b close to e to indicate the remaining, uncounted tail. Designed for iterative processing over large buffers.
requirements: Declared only when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2; implemented for AVX-512BW-capable builds.
b must reference a valid pointer into a readable memory buffer; e must point to the end of the same buffer, with b <= e.

Caller should expect b to be updated (advanced) on return and must use the updated b for subsequent calls.

functions.description: AVX2-accelerated partial UTF-8 validator. Checks whether the bytes in [b, e) conform to UTF-8 (implementation-specific details unknown) and advances b to the position of any remaining, unvalidated tail. The exact advancement policy is not documented in this header.
requirements: Declared only when building with one of HAVE_AVX512BW, HAVE_AVX2, or HAVE_SSE2; implemented for AVX2-capable builds.
b must reference a valid pointer into a readable memory buffer; e must point to the end of the same buffer, with b <= e.
The memory range [b, e) must be accessible for reading.
Caller should expect b to be updated (advanced) on return and must use the updated b for subsequent calls.

functions.name: reflex::nlcount
functions.signature: extern size_t reflex::nlcount(const char *s, const char *e)
functions.description: Counts newline characters in the memory range [s, e). Intended for scanning a buffer segment up to position e.
requirements: s and e must point into the same readable buffer with s <= e.
The memory range [s, e) must be accessible for reading.

functions.name: reflex::isutf8
functions.signature: extern bool reflex::isutf8(const char *s, const char *e)
functions.description: Checks whether the memory range [s, e) is valid UTF-8 and does not contain a NUL byte, but accepts surrogate code points and 3/4-byte overlong sequences as valid. Exact rejection/acceptance follows the implementation; only these notes are documented here.
requirements: s and e must point into the same readable buffer with s <= e.
The memory range [s, e) must be accessible for reading.

functions.name: reflex::Input::Input
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty Input with no source assigned. After construction, init() is called to reset internal state.

functions.description: Copy-assigns Input, sharing underlying state with the source (intended move-like semantics). Using both objects to read afterwards is undefined behavior.

functions.name: reflex::Input::operator const char *
functions.description: Implicit cast returning the remaining unbuffered portion of the NUL-terminated char string, or NULL if the Input is not a char-string source.

The returned pointer becomes invalid if the Input source changes or progresses due to reading.

functions.name: reflex::Input::operator const wchar_t *

functions.name: reflex::Input::operator FILE *
functions.description: Implicit cast returning the current FILE* or NULL if the Input is not a FILE* source.
requirements: Use only if the Input currently represents a FILE* source.
The returned FILE* is owned/closed by the caller if the caller originally supplied it; Input does not close it automatically.

functions.name: reflex::Input::operator std::istream *
functions.description: Implicit cast returning the current std::istream* or NULL if the Input is not a stream source.
requirements: Use only if the Input currently represents a std::istream source.

functions.name: reflex::Input::operator bool
functions.description: Boolean test equivalent to good(). Returns true if a non-empty sequence of characters is available to get.
requirements: None beyond good().

functions.name: reflex::Input::cstring
functions.description: Returns the remaining unbuffered part of the NUL-terminated char string if this Input is a char-string source, otherwise NULL.
requirements: Only meaningful when Input was constructed from a char string.

functions.name: reflex::Input::wstring
functions.description: Returns the remaining unbuffered part of the NUL-terminated wide string if this Input is a wide-string source, otherwise NULL.
requirements: Only meaningful when Input was constructed from a wide string.

functions.name: reflex::Input::file
functions.description: Returns the underlying FILE* if this Input is a FILE* source, otherwise NULL.
requirements: Only meaningful when Input was constructed from a FILE*.

functions.name: reflex::Input::istream
functions.description: Returns the underlying std::istream* if this Input is a stream source, otherwise NULL.
requirements: Only meaningful when Input was constructed from a std::istream.

functions.name: reflex::Input::size
functions.description: Returns the number of ASCII/UTF-8 bytes available to read from the source, or zero if empty or indeterminable (e.g., for std::istream). For wide strings and UTF-16/32 files, returns the number of UTF-8 bytes that will be produced by get(). Should be called before reading.
requirements: Call size() before reading to obtain a meaningful total; reading progresses internal position and may change what remains.
For std::istream sources, size may be zero because size cannot be determined.
For FILE* sources, size may trigger BOM detection and may read file content to compute UTF-8 size for UTF-16/32 files (per comments).

functions.name: reflex::Input::assigned
functions.description: Returns true if this Input has any source assigned (string, wide string, FILE*, or stream).
requirements: None.

functions.name: reflex::Input::clear
functions.description: Clears/unassigns the Input source and resets size to 0.
requirements: After clear(), the Input has no source; good() will be false and eof() true.

functions.name: reflex::Input::good
functions.description: Checks if the input is readable and has no EOF or error. For strings, equivalent to size remaining > 0; for FILE* checks !feof && !ferror; for streams uses istream.good().
requirements: For FILE* and streams, good() may be false due to errors even before eof().

functions.name: reflex::Input::eof
functions.description: Returns true if the input reached EOF and no characters are available. For strings, eof() == !good(); for FILE*/streams, eof() implies good()==false but not vice versa.
requirements: None.

functions.name: reflex::Input::get
functions.description: Reads and returns one byte as an unsigned char promoted to int (0..255). Returns EOF (-1) on end-of-input or error. Converts from wide sources to UTF-8 as needed.

Use eof()/good() to distinguish EOF from error when needed.

functions.description: Sets the encoding for FILE* input. When a BOM is present, auto-detection may override this. For custom encoding, a code page can be supplied.

If enc is file_encoding::custom, a valid page pointer should be provided (format unspecified here).

functions.description: Initializes internal state after (re)setting the input source. For FILE* sources, calls file_init() to possibly auto-detect BOM/encoding.

functions.name: reflex::Input::file_init
functions.description: Initializes FILE* handling, including BOM auto-detection if file size is known. Implementation not shown in this header.
requirements: A valid FILE* must be set before calling.
Behavioral details are implementation-defined (unknown in this header).

functions.name: reflex::Input::wstring_size
functions.description: Computes and caches the size (in UTF-8 bytes) for wide-string sources. Implementation not shown in this header.
requirements: A valid wide-string source must be set before calling.

functions.name: reflex::Input::file_size
functions.description: Determines and caches the size (in UTF-8 bytes) for FILE* sources, accounting for BOM/encoding. Implementation not shown in this header.
requirements: A valid FILE* must be set before calling.
May read the file content to compute UTF-8 byte size for UTF-16/32 files as per class documentation.

functions.description: Attempts to determine the size for std::istream sources. Often indeterminable; implementation not shown here.
requirements: A valid std::istream must be set before calling.

A valid FILE* must be set before calling.

functions.description: Reads exactly n bytes into buffer s from FILE*, blocking as needed (using file_ready() when non-blocking). Returns true on success, false on fewer bytes (failure or EOF).

A valid FILE* must be set; returns false immediately if file_ is NULL.

functions.name: reflex::Input::file_ready
functions.description: Waits for non-blocking FILE* input to be ready and returns true, or returns false for EOF or errors (ignores EINTR). Implementation not shown in this header.
requirements: A valid FILE* must be set before calling.

functions.name: reflex::Input::set_handler
functions.description: Sets a handler functor that is invoked after file_get() reads data from a FILE*. The handler can analyze/modify the buffer and control how many bytes are consumed.

Handler may modify the buffer pointer and contents as documented in the Handler comment.

functions.name: reflex::Input::dos_streambuf::showmanyc

requirements: None.

functions.description: Assigns from an unbuffered Input, sharing its state, and refills the buffer with up to SIZE bytes.

functions.description: Returns true if there is buffered data remaining or the underlying Input reports good().
requirements: None.

functions.description: Returns true if the buffer is exhausted and the underlying Input is at EOF.
requirements: None.

functions.description: Peeks the next byte without consuming it, refilling the buffer from the underlying Input as needed. Returns EOF on end-of-input.

functions.name: reflex::BufferedInput::get
functions.description: Gets the next byte, refilling the buffer from the underlying Input as needed. Returns EOF on end-of-input.

functions.name: reflex::BufferedInput::streambuf::streambuf
functions.description: Constructs a buffered std::streambuf over a BufferedInput, suitable for std::istream.

functions.name: REFLEX_DBGOUT_
functions.signature: extern "C" void REFLEX_DBGOUT_(const char *log, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Initializes/updates the debug output destination and begins a new log entry for RE/flex debug macros. It is invoked by the DBGLOG/DBGLOGN/DBGLOGA macros to prepare REFLEX_DBGFD_ and to emit the log-entry prefix (e.g., timestamp and source file:line) before the formatted message is written. Typical usage is indirect via the debug macros; direct calls are uncommon and intended for internal use.
requirements: log must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string naming the log destination as determined by the macros (e.g., "DEBUG.log" or a name derived from the DEBUG macro).
file must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string, normally passed as __FILE__.
line should be the corresponding source line number, normally passed as __LINE__ (non-negative integer).
Callers should normally not invoke this function directly; use DBGLOG/DBGLOGN/DBGLOGA which pass correct arguments and manage REFLEX_DBGFD_.
If called directly, the caller must ensure subsequent writes use REFLEX_DBGFD_ and handle flushing as needed (the macros call fprintf/fflush after REFLEX_DBGOUT_).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented; concurrent calls may interleave output (unknown).

functions.name: reflex::regex_error::pos
functions.description: Accessor that returns the position index within the pattern at which the error was detected when this regex_error was created. Use to locate the error in the original pattern for diagnostics or highlighting.
requirements: Must be called on a valid reflex::regex_error instance (may be const).
The returned index relates to the pattern string provided at construction; interpretation of multibyte encodings is not specified here.

functions.name: reflex::convert
functions.signature: std::string reflex::convert(const char *pattern, const char *signature, reflex::convert_flag_type flags = reflex::convert_flag::none, bool *multiline = NULL, const std::map<std::string,std::string> *macros = NULL)
functions.description: Converts a regex pattern to the target library’s syntax according to a compact capability signature and conversion flags. Expands optional {name} macros and reports via the multiline pointer if the resulting pattern may span multiple lines. Throws regex_error on invalid input or unsupported constructs. Typical use: adapt user/lexer patterns to an engine (as described by the signature string) while applying flags such as basic, unicode, anycase, multiline, dotall, freespace, etc.
requirements: pattern must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer (non-null)

signature must be a valid, null-terminated C string in the form "decls:escapes?+." with optional parts: a pre-':' declarations block (modifiers and special (?...) constructs), a ':' followed by supported escape letters, optional '?' and/or '+' to indicate lazy/possessive quantifier support, optional '.' to indicate dot matches any char except newline, and optional '[' to indicate character class set operations support

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate interesting arbitrary byte strings to be used as both regex patterns
# and input texts by the fuzz stubs. The stubs cap lengths and accept any bytes.
# Strategy:
# - Construct inputs that often yield matches for various regexes (letters, digits,
#   whitespace, word/non-word boundaries, lines with/without newlines, CRLF, UTF-8
#   and non-UTF-8 sequences, NULs, long runs, punctuation, etc.).
# - Include substrings that common regexes from stubs may use: dots, literals, groups,
#   anchors, word characters, spaces, digits, line starts/ends.
# - Keep overall size modest (< 4096 bytes).
# - Randomize composition based on seed while ensuring validity and diversity.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"hello", b"world", b"test", b"regex", b"match", b"group", b"alpha", b"beta",
    b"gamma", b"delta", b"epsilon", b"zeta", b"theta", b"kappa", b"lambda",
]
DIGITS = [bytes(str(i), 'ascii') for i in range(10)]
PUNCT = [b".", b",", b";", b":", b"!", b"?", b"(", b")", b"[", b"]", b"{", b"}", b"+", b"*", b"|", b"^"]
SPACES = [b" ", b"\t"]
NEWLINES = [b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\r"]

# Some valid UTF-8 sequences for non-ASCII coverage
UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    " café ".encode('utf-8'),
    "naïve".encode('utf-8'),
    "日本語".encode('utf-8'),
    "🙂".encode('utf-8'),
    "Привет".encode('utf-8'),
]

# Some invalid UTF-8 byte sequences to exercise binary paths
INVALID_UTF8 = [
    b"\xC0\xAF",   # overlong /
    b"\xE0\x80",    # truncated 3-byte
    b"\xF0\x80\x80",# truncated 4-byte
    b"\x80",        # lone continuation
]

# Snippets that help line/column logic
LINE_SNIPPETS = [
    b"first line\nsecond line\nthird line\n",
    b"line with tabs\t\tcolumns\n",
    b"empty\n\nlines\n",
]

# Repetitions to trigger more(), less(), size/first/last boundaries
RUNS = [b"a"*n for n in (1,2,3,4,8,16,32)] + [b"0"*10, b"x"*5 + b"y"*5]

# Substrings helpful for StdMatcher capture tests
CAPTURE_FRIENDLY = [b"aaabbbccc", b"xxyyzz", b"abc123", b"word boundary"]

# Include NULs and binary noise
BINARY_NOISE = [
    b"\x00", b"\x00\x00", b"\x00A\x00B", bytes([0,255,0,128,10]),
]

# CRLF normalization coverage
CRLF_SNIPS = [b"win\r\nline\r\nend\r\n", b"mixed\ncrlf\r\nlf\n"]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[bytes], k: int) -> List[bytes]:
    if not items:
        return []
    # sample with replacement to keep size flexible
    return [rng.choice(items) for _ in range(k)]


def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/.,;!?'()[]{}|+*^$\t\n"
    return bytes(''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)), 'utf-8')


def _build_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Optional BOM or encoding markers to exercise Input encoding logic
    bom_choices = [b"", b"\xEF\xBB\xBF", b"\xFF\xFE", b"\xFE\xFF"]
    parts.append(rng.choice(bom_choices))

    # Start with some words and digits to enable simple patterns to match
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, ASCII_WORDS, rng.randint(2, 6))
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, DIGITS, rng.randint(3, 8))

    # Insert punctuation and spaces
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, PUNCT, rng.randint(3, 10))
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, SPACES, rng.randint(3, 8))

    # Lines content including CRLF and LF
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, LINE_SNIPPETS, rng.randint(1, 3))
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, CRLF_SNIPS, rng.randint(0, 2))

    # UTF-8 and invalid UTF-8 chunks
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, UTF8_SNIPPETS, rng.randint(1, 3))
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, INVALID_UTF8, rng.randint(0, 2))

    # Runs and capture-friendly strings
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, RUNS, rng.randint(2, 5))
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, CAPTURE_FRIENDLY, rng.randint(1, 3))

    # Sprinkle some binary noise including NULs
    parts += _rand_choice(rng, BINARY_NOISE, rng.randint(1, 3))

    # Random ASCII filler with newlines to influence line/column
    parts.append(_random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(20, 80)))

    # Ensure at least one newline near end for eol()/lineno_end() paths
    parts.append(b"\n")

    # Optionally add a large block of repeating characters to test fetch/avail
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ch = rng.choice([b"A", b"B", b"C", b" ", b"\t", b"x"])  # simple bytes
        parts.append(ch * rng.randint(32, 256))

    # Optionally terminate with CRLF as well
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(b"\r\n")

    # Shuffle mid-sections for variety but keep BOM at front
    core = parts[1:]
    rng.shuffle(core)
    data = parts[0] + b"".join(core)

    # Cap to 4096 bytes as requested
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    # Ensure non-empty (stubs expect non-empty often)
    if not data:
        data = b"a\n"
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_buffer(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target format: UTF-8 text
# We generate interesting yet valid UTF-8 byte sequences that help the stubs:
# - regex patterns (<=64 bytes) to promote matches
# - data blobs (<=512 bytes) that contain lines, various Unicode ranges,
#   ASCII, boundaries, combining marks, surrogate-like code points excluded,
#   mixed scripts, and well-formed multibyte sequences.
# The fuzzer infra will request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffers; we supply one
# initial shared seed buffer that encodes two concatenated sections separated by
# NULs so the harness can obtain different slices. However, we keep the buffer
# as a single valid UTF-8 text overall: we do not embed NUL inside multi-byte.
#
# Layout we produce (all UTF-8-valid bytes):
#   [pattern]\n\n[data]
# The consumer will slice as needed; both parts are individually valid UTF-8.
# We keep total size <= 4096.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "a", "ab", "abc", "word", "line", "test", "data", "match",
    "hello", "world", "foo", "bar", "baz", "qux",
]

REGEX_SNIPPETS = [
    ".*", ".+", "?", "^", "$", "^.*$", "[A-Za-z]+", "[0-9]+",
    "\\w+", "\\W+", "\\s*", "\\S+", "(?:ab)+", "(hello)",
    "(\u00E9)",  # é
    "(\xF0\x9F\x98\x80)",  # 😀 as raw UTF-8 bytes escape, still valid as pattern text
]

# Representative Unicode code point classes to include in data:
UNICODE_RANGES: List[Tuple[int, int]] = [
    (0x20, 0x7E),       # printable ASCII
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 supplement
    (0x0100, 0x017F),   # Latin Extended-A
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
    (0x0590, 0x05FF),   # Hebrew
    (0x0600, 0x06FF),   # Arabic
    (0x0900, 0x097F),   # Devanagari
    (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
    (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
    (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs (BMP)
    (0x1F300, 0x1F6FF), # Misc Symbols and Pictographs (emoji range)
]

COMBINING_MARKS = list(range(0x0300, 0x036F + 1))

def utf8_encode_codepoint(cp: int) -> bytes:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return bytes([cp])
    elif cp < 0x800:
        return bytes([
            0xC0 | (cp >> 6),
            0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)
        ])
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        # Exclude surrogates
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0xFFFD
        return bytes([
            0xE0 | (cp >> 12),
            0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
            0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)
        ])
    else:
        if cp > 0x10FFFF:
            cp = 0x10FFFF
        return bytes([
            0xF0 | (cp >> 18),
            0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F),
            0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
            0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)
        ])

def rand_cp(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Weighted: mostly BMP/ASCII with some astral
    roll = r.random()
    if roll < 0.6:
        rng = (0x20, 0x7E)
    elif roll < 0.8:
        rng = r.choice(UNICODE_RANGES[:6])
    elif roll < 0.95:
        rng = r.choice(UNICODE_RANGES)
    else:
        rng = (0x1F300, 0x1FAFF)
    lo, hi = rng
    cp = r.randint(lo, hi)
    # Avoid surrogates
    if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
        cp = 0xFFFD
    return cp

def make_regex(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Build a regex that is likely to match our data:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Start with a literal or simple class
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        lit = r.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        parts.append(lit)
    else:
        parts.append(r.choice(["[A-Za-z]+", "[\u00C0-\u017F]+", "[\p{L}]+"]))
    # Optionally add anchors/quantifiers/groups
    extras = r.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(extras):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.35:
            parts.append(r.choice([".*", ".+", "\\s*", "\\S+", "?", "+"]))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            parts.append(r.choice(["^", "$", "^.*$"]))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(["(\\w+)", "(hello)", "(?:ab)+"]))
    # Sometimes add a specific UTF-8 literal like emoji or accented char
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(r.choice(["é", "ñ", "ü", "😀", "Ω"]))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Truncate to byte limit safely (UTF-8 aware)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')[:max_len]
    # Ensure we don't cut mid-sequence
    while b and (b[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        b = b[:-1]
    try:
        return b.decode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    except Exception:
        return "a.*"  # Fallback simple matcher

def make_line(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a single line without newlines, mixing scripts and combining marks
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        mode = r.random()
        if mode < 0.65:
            cp = rand_cp(r)
            out += utf8_encode_codepoint(cp)
            # maybe add combining marks
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                for _ in range(r.randint(1, 2)):
                    out += utf8_encode_codepoint(r.choice(COMBINING_MARKS))
        elif mode < 0.8:
            # ASCII word
            w = r.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
            out += w.encode('utf-8')
        else:
            # digits or punctuation
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                out += bytes([ord('0') + r.randint(0, 9)])
            else:
                out += r.choice([b" ", b"\t", b"-", b"_", b".", b",", b";"])
    # Trim to target_len without cutting UTF-8
    out = out[:target_len]
    while out and (out[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        out = out[:-1]
    return bytes(out)

def make_data(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build multi-line data, include empty lines and CRLF variants
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    num = r.randint(3, 10)
    for i in range(num):
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            line = b""  # empty line
        else:
            target = r.randint(5, min(80, max_len // max(1, num)))
            line = make_line(r, target)
        # choose newline style
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            nl = b"\r\n"
        else:
            nl = b"\n"
        lines.append(line + nl)
    blob = b"".join(lines)
    # ensure max_len
    blob = blob[:max_len]
    # avoid ending mid-UTF-8 sequence
    while blob and (blob[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        blob = blob[:-1]
    return blob

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Construct pattern and data; total budget <= 4096
    pattern = make_regex(r, 64)
    data = make_data(r, 512)

    # Include sections that some stubs use directly as data without matching
    # Append a short prefix to help winput()/wunput() consume valid code points
    prefix_cps = [0x0061, 0x00E9, 0x03A9, 0x1F600]  # a, é, Ω, 😀
    prefix = b"".join(utf8_encode_codepoint(cp) for cp in prefix_cps)

    # Assemble final buffer: pattern, double newline separator, then prefix+data
    sep = b"\n\n"
    out = pattern.encode('utf-8') + sep + prefix + b"\n" + data

    # Final safety: cap and avoid partial UTF-8 at end
    out = out[:4096]
    while out and (out[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        out = out[:-1]
    if not out:
        out = b"a\n"
    return out
